passages.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, To the twelve tribes of the Dispersion: Greetings.
passages.original: Ἰάκωβος Θεοῦ καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ δοῦλος Ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ Διασπορᾷ Χαίρειν
passages.objections:
Why should I listen to someone who claims to serve both God and Jesus? Aren’t they different?
I don’t see why anyone outside of Jerusalem would care about these messages.
If we’re scattered and far from home, doesn’t that mean God has forgotten us?
How can someone speak with authority to all twelve tribes when we’re so divided?
Why should I trust a letter from someone I’ve never met?
Isn’t it pointless to greet people who are suffering in exile?
If James is just a servant, what makes his words important?
Why would God care about people living among foreigners?
Aren’t we too far gone for any message to matter now?
How can anyone claim to represent both God and Jesus at the same time?

passages.text: Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds, because you know that the testing of your faith develops perseverance.
passages.original: Πᾶσαν χαρὰν ἡγήσασθε ἀδελφοί μου ὅταν πειρασμοῖς περιπέσητε ποικίλοις γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν
passages.objections:
I don't see how anything good can come from the troubles I'm facing right now.
Why should I be happy when life gets hard? That doesn't make any sense.
If I'm struggling, it must mean that God is upset with me or has abandoned me.
There's no purpose to suffering—it's just pointless pain.
If my faith is strong, I shouldn't have to go through any difficulties at all.
I can't imagine ever feeling joy when everything seems to be falling apart.
Trials just make people bitter and hopeless, not stronger.
If God really cared, He would keep me from experiencing any hardships.
Enduring tough times doesn't change anything for the better.
I think it's impossible to grow or learn anything valuable from suffering.

passages.text: Allow perseverance to finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ ὑπομονὴ ἔργον τέλειον ἐχέτω ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι ἐν μηδενὶ λειπόμενοι
passages.objections:
I don’t see how being patient through hard times could ever make me a better person.
Why should I keep going when things get tough? It just feels pointless.
If I’m struggling, it must mean I’m doing something wrong or that I’m not good enough.
There’s no way that enduring difficulties could actually help me grow or improve.
I think it’s better to avoid challenges altogether instead of trying to push through them.
How can waiting and persevering possibly lead to anything good?
If I’m lacking something, it means I’ll always be incomplete, no matter what I do.
I don’t believe that patience can really change who I am or make me whole.
Why should I trust that sticking it out will ever make me feel satisfied or fulfilled?
It seems like nothing good ever comes from just enduring hardship.

passages.text: Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας αἰτείτω παρὰ τοῦ διδόντος Θεοῦ πᾶσιν ἁπλῶς καὶ μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ
passages.objections:
I don’t think God cares enough to help me understand things.
I’m too ashamed to ask God for wisdom after all my mistakes.
Maybe God only gives wisdom to special people, not to someone like me.
I’ve asked for help before, but I don’t think God wants to answer me.
I’m not smart enough for God to give me any real insight.
God probably gets annoyed when I keep asking for guidance.
I have to figure everything out on my own because God won’t help.
If I don’t already have wisdom, it’s too late for me to get it now.
God is too busy with bigger problems to listen to my requests.
I’m afraid God will judge me for not knowing what to do.

passages.text: But he must ask in faith, without doubting, because he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.
passages.original: αἰτείτω δὲ ἐν πίστει μηδὲν διακρινόμενος ὁ γὰρ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ
passages.objections:
I don’t think it matters if I really believe when I pray—God will answer anyway.
Sometimes I just ask, but deep down I’m not sure God is even listening.
Isn’t it normal to always question whether God will actually help me?
I can pray, but I don’t see why I need to trust that anything will happen.
Maybe God only helps people who are perfect in their faith, not someone like me who’s always unsure.
I’ll just try praying, but I doubt anything will change.
Why should I expect God to do anything for me if I’m not convinced He will?
I don’t see the harm in being skeptical when I ask God for something.
Faith is just a feeling—if I don’t have it, my prayers should still count, right?
I can’t help but waver back and forth; it’s just who I am.

passages.text: That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.
passages.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰέσθω ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου
passages.objections:
I can just ask God for things even if I don’t really believe He’ll answer me.
It doesn’t matter if I doubt; God will still give me what I want.
I don’t need to trust God fully—He’ll help me anyway.
I can be unsure about God and still expect Him to bless me.
Even if my faith wavers all the time, God will always give me what I ask for.
It’s fine to be double-minded; God doesn’t care about that.
I can pray without really believing, and God will still answer.
God gives to everyone, even if they don’t trust Him at all.
My attitude when I ask God doesn’t matter; He’ll give me things regardless.

passages.text: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
passages.original: ἀνὴρ δίψυχος ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ὁδοῖς αὐτοῦ
passages.objections:
I can believe two different things at once and still be steady in my life.
It's fine to keep changing my mind about what I trust; it doesn't affect my actions.
I can follow God and chase after other things at the same time without any trouble.
Doubt and indecision don't really make me unstable; I can handle it.
As long as I do good things, it doesn't matter if my heart is divided.
I don't need to be fully committed; wavering a little is normal and harmless.
Being unsure about my faith won't cause any problems in my daily life.
I can serve two masters and still be consistent in everything I do.
It's okay to be half-hearted; it won't make me unreliable.
My choices don't get affected by my divided loyalties.

passages.text: The brother in humble circumstances should exult in his high position.
passages.original: Καυχάσθω δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ
passages.objections:
Why should someone who’s poor or lowly feel proud or important? 
If you’re not wealthy or powerful, you don’t really matter in this world.
Only those with status and riches have anything to celebrate.
There’s nothing special about being humble or having little.
People in low positions should be ashamed, not joyful.
If you’re struggling, it means you’ve failed and have nothing to boast about.
No one respects someone who’s at the bottom; why should they rejoice?
You can’t have dignity if you don’t have money or influence.
Being humble just means you’re overlooked and forgotten.
How can someone with nothing see themselves as having any worth?

passages.text: But the one who is rich should exult in his low position, because he will pass away like a flower of the field.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ ὅτι ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου παρελεύσεται
passages.objections:
If I have enough money, I’ll always be secure and important.
Wealth means I’m better than those who have less.
As long as I’m rich, I don’t need to worry about anything changing.
My riches prove that I’m favored and will always be on top.
I don’t see why I should ever humble myself if I have everything I want.
Rich people are untouchable and their success lasts forever.
If I’m wealthy, I don’t need to think about my life ending or losing what I have.
There’s no reason for someone with riches to feel low or insignificant.
Money guarantees my legacy and lasting influence.
I can rely on my wealth to get me through anything.

passages.text: For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the plant; its flower falls and its beauty is lost. So too, the rich man will fade away in the midst of his pursuits.
passages.original: ἀνέτειλεν γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον καὶ τὸ ἄνθος αὐτοῦ ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ ἀπώλετο οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν ταῖς πορείαις αὐτοῦ μαρανθήσεται
passages.objections:
Wealth will protect me from any hardship or trouble.
If I have enough money, I’ll always be important and admired.
Rich people are secure and their success will last forever.
As long as I keep gaining more, I’ll never lose what I have.
My possessions and status prove that I’m favored and untouchable.
I don’t need to worry about the future because my riches guarantee it.
The powerful and wealthy are above the struggles that others face.
If I work hard and become rich, I’ll never have to fear losing anything.
My achievements and beauty will never fade as long as I’m prosperous.

passages.text: Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial, because when he has stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him.
passages.original: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν ὅτι δόκιμος γενόμενος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν
passages.objections:
I don’t see any point in enduring hardships—nothing good ever comes from suffering.
If God really loved us, He wouldn’t let us go through tough times at all.
Only people who have an easy life are truly blessed.
There’s no reward for sticking it out when things get hard; it’s just pointless pain.
God must have forgotten about me since I’m struggling so much.
If I’m facing trials, it must mean I’ve done something wrong and God is punishing me.
No one can really make it through temptation or suffering; it’s impossible to stay faithful.
Why should I keep loving God if He lets me suffer?
Enduring trials doesn’t matter—what counts is how successful or comfortable I am right now.

passages.text: When tempted, no one should say, “God is tempting me.” For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.
passages.original: Μηδεὶς πειραζόμενος λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πειράζομαι ὁ γὰρ Θεὸς ἀπείραστός ἐστιν κακῶν πειράζει δὲ αὐτὸς οὐδένα
passages.objections:
I think God is the one making me want to do wrong things.
If I’m struggling with temptation, it must be because God is testing me to see if I’ll fail.
God must be trying to trip me up so He can punish me later.
Whenever I feel tempted, it’s because God put those desires in my heart.
If I fall into sin, it’s really God’s fault for putting me in that situation.
God sometimes wants us to do bad things just to see what we’ll choose.
I can’t help it if I sin—God is the one who made me this way.
God is tempting me on purpose to make my life harder.
If God didn’t want me to sin, He wouldn’t let me be tempted at all.
It’s not my responsibility if I give in to temptation, because God is in control of everything.

passages.text: But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.
passages.original: ἕκαστος δὲ πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος
passages.objections:
It’s not my fault I keep messing up—someone else must be making me do it.
I can’t help it if I give in to temptation; it’s just the way things are.
Evil thoughts just come from nowhere, and I have no control over them.
If I do something wrong, it must be because of bad luck or fate.
I only sin because other people lead me astray, not because of anything inside me.
There’s no way my own desires could be the problem; it has to be something outside of me.
I’m not responsible for my actions when I’m tempted—it’s out of my hands.
If I feel tempted, it must be because God is testing me, not because of my own heart.
I wouldn’t do anything wrong if the world wasn’t so corrupt; it’s not about me.
Temptation is always someone else’s fault, never mine.

passages.text: Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.
passages.original: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν ἡ δὲ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον
passages.objections:
I don’t see how just wanting something could ever lead to real trouble.
Sin isn’t really that serious—it’s just a mistake, nothing more.
As long as I don’t act on my desires, they can’t hurt anyone.
Everyone gives in to temptation sometimes; it’s not like it has any lasting consequences.
If something feels good, it can’t possibly be wrong for me.
Sin is just an old-fashioned idea; it doesn’t actually lead to anything bad.
I can always fix things later, so it doesn’t matter if I mess up now.
Desires are natural, so following them can’t be harmful.
There’s no real danger in letting my thoughts run wild—what’s the worst that could happen?
I don’t believe that small sins can ever lead to anything as serious as death.

passages.text: Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
passages.original: Μὴ πλανᾶσθε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί
passages.objections:
I don’t think it really matters if I’m a little careless with what I believe—nothing bad will come of it.
Everyone else seems to think this way, so it must be right.
I can’t be tricked or led astray; I know everything I need to know.
If something feels good or sounds true, I should just go with it.
There’s no harm in following my own ideas, even if they don’t match what I was taught.
I don’t need to worry about being deceived; I’m too smart for that.
It’s impossible for good people like us to be misled.
If I make a mistake in what I believe, it won’t really affect my life.
I don’t need to double-check what I hear or read; I can trust my instincts.
Deception only happens to people who aren’t paying attention, and I’m always alert.

passages.text: Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, with whom there is no change or shifting shadow.
passages.original: πᾶσα δόσις ἀγαθὴ καὶ πᾶν δώρημα τέλειον ἄνωθέν ἐστιν καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ Πατρὸς τῶν φώτων παρ’ ᾧ οὐκ ἔνι παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα
passages.objections:
I think all the good things in my life just come from luck or my own hard work.
Maybe the blessings I have are just random, not from any higher power.
God probably changes His mind about people all the time, so I can’t trust Him to be consistent.
Some gifts in life are good, but others must come from somewhere else, not from God.
I feel like God gives good things to some people but not to everyone, so He must play favorites.
Isn’t it possible that God sometimes gives us bad things just to test us?
I don’t see how anything perfect could come from above when the world is so messed up.
Maybe God used to give good gifts, but He doesn’t do that anymore.
I think the universe just runs on its own, and God isn’t really involved in what happens to us.
If God really cared, wouldn’t He change His ways to fit what we want or need?

passages.text: He chose to give us birth through the word of truth, that we would be a kind of firstfruits of His creation.
passages.original: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας εἰς τὸ εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἀπαρχήν τινα τῶν αὐτοῦ κτισμάτων
passages.objections:
I don’t think God really cares about us more than anything else He made.
We just happened by chance; there’s nothing special about people compared to the rest of creation.
God probably didn’t have any plan for us from the beginning.
Maybe we have to earn our place with God by our own efforts.
I doubt there’s any real purpose for us being here.
God treats everyone and everything exactly the same, so humans aren’t unique at all.
We can’t really know if God wants us to be close to Him.
Truth is just whatever we decide, not something God gives us.
I don’t see how God could choose anyone in particular for anything special.

passages.text: My beloved brothers, understand this: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger, for man’s anger does not bring about the righteousness that God desires.
passages.original: Ἴστε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοί ἔστω δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν ὀργὴ γὰρ ἀνδρὸς δικαιοσύνην Θεοῦ οὐκ ἐργάζεται
passages.objections:
If someone insults me, I have every right to snap back at them right away.
I can't help but get angry quickly—it's just who I am.
If I don't speak up immediately, people will walk all over me.
Getting angry is the only way to show people I'm serious.
Why should I bother listening to others when I already know I'm right?
If I don't vent my anger, I'll never get justice.
It's pointless to hold back my words; people need to hear what I think right now.
Anger is a good thing—it motivates me to do what's right.
There's no harm in losing my temper every now and then.
Listening to others just wastes time when I could be making my point.

passages.text: Therefore, get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil, and humbly accept the word planted in you, which can save your souls.
passages.original: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν ἔμφυτον λόγον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν
passages.objections:
I don’t see why I need to change my behavior; everyone does bad things sometimes.
Why should I get rid of my old habits if they make me happy?
I think I can figure out life on my own without anyone telling me what’s right or wrong.
Isn’t it enough just to believe in something? Why do I have to accept anything new?
I don’t think words or teachings can really change who I am inside.
If I’m already a good person, why do I need to worry about evil or filth?
Why should I be humble about what I believe? I know what’s best for me.
I don’t see how anything planted in me could actually save my soul.
Can’t I just live however I want and still be fine in the end?
Isn’t it too late for me to get rid of all the bad things I’ve done?

passages.text: Be doers of the word, and not hearers only. Otherwise, you are deceiving yourselves.
passages.original: Γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς
passages.objections:
Why should I bother actually doing anything if I already know what’s right?
Isn’t it enough just to listen to good teachings and agree with them in my heart?
I don’t need to change my actions as long as I believe the right things.
Hearing the word is all that matters—God knows my intentions.
As long as I go to church and listen, I’m doing my part.
I can just think about what’s good and that’s enough for God.
Obeying is too hard; understanding is what really counts.
I don’t need to put these teachings into practice—just knowing them is fine.
My faith is private, so I don’t have to show it by what I do.
Actions aren’t important as long as I have faith in my heart.

passages.text: For anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out is like a man who looks at his face in a mirror, and after observing himself goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.
passages.original: ὅτι εἴ τις ἀκροατὴς λόγου ἐστὶν καὶ οὐ ποιητής οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ πρόσωπον τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ κατενόησεν γὰρ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν
passages.objections:
I think just listening to good teachings is enough for me to be right with God.
Isn’t it enough to know what’s right, even if I don’t always do it?
I hear the sermons every week, so I’m sure I’m growing spiritually.
As long as I agree with what’s being taught, I don’t need to change anything in my life.
Why should I bother putting these lessons into practice? Understanding them is what matters most.
I don’t see the harm in just listening and not acting; at least I’m learning.
Isn’t faith just about believing and hearing, not necessarily doing?
I remember what I hear for a while, but it’s not a big deal if I forget to live it out.
If I know the right thing in my heart, my actions don’t really matter, do they?
I’m sure God is pleased as long as I pay attention during the readings, even if I don’t follow through.

passages.text: But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so—not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer—he will be blessed in what he does.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ παρακύψας εἰς νόμον τέλειον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας οὐκ ἀκροατὴς ἐπιλησμονῆς γενόμενος ἀλλὰ ποιητὴς ἔργου οὗτος μακάριος ἐν τῇ ποιήσει αὐτοῦ ἔσται
passages.objections:
I think just knowing the right things is enough; I don’t actually have to do anything about it.
Isn’t it enough to just listen to good teachings and agree with them in my heart?
Why should I keep trying to follow these commands? Nothing really changes for me anyway.
I don’t see how actually living out these teachings makes any difference in my life.
As long as I remember what’s right, I don’t need to act on it every time.
Isn’t faith just about believing, not about doing?
I can’t see how obeying these rules brings any real blessing.
Why bother putting in the effort to keep following this law? It seems pointless.
I think I can just pick and choose when to act; it doesn’t matter if I’m consistent.

passages.text: If anyone considers himself religious and yet does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his heart and his religion is worthless.
passages.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ θρησκὸς εἶναι μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν γλῶσσαν αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ τούτου μάταιος ἡ θρησκεία
passages.objections:
I can say whatever I want as long as I go to worship and follow the rituals.
It doesn’t matter if I gossip or insult others; my faith is still strong.
As long as I believe the right things, my words don’t really matter.
I can’t help it if I lose my temper and speak harshly—everyone does it.
My religion is about what I do in the temple, not how I talk to people.
It’s not a big deal if I lie or curse sometimes; nobody’s perfect.
I’m still a good person even if I spread rumors or speak badly about others.
Controlling my tongue isn’t important for my relationship with God.
My words don’t affect my spiritual life as long as I pray and give offerings.
I can’t see how my speech has anything to do with my faith.

passages.text: Pure and undefiled religion before our God and Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.
passages.original: θρησκεία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ αὕτη ἐστίν ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν τῇ θλίψει αὐτῶν ἄσπιλον ἑαυτὸν τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου
passages.objections:
I think as long as I go to church and say my prayers, that’s all God really wants from me.
Helping people in need isn’t really my responsibility; someone else will take care of them.
It doesn’t matter how I live during the week as long as I believe the right things.
Why should I worry about staying away from the world’s ways? Everyone else is doing it.
I don’t see why I should bother with orphans and widows—they’re not my family.
My faith is private, so I don’t need to get involved in other people’s problems.
As long as I give a little money, I don’t need to actually visit or help anyone.
God only cares about my heart, not about what I do for others.
It’s impossible to stay pure in this world, so why even try?
Religion is just about rituals and traditions, not about helping people.
